rows.text: Before an overdraft fee is charged on a card or app transaction, a firm must show the consumer the fee amount and give a choice to cancel the transaction.
rows.controlDesc: App release test confirms the overdraft fee prompt and cancel option appear before a fee-bearing transaction
rows.reason: Policy POL-FEE-01 states "Before an overdraft fee is charged on a card or app transaction, the app shows the fee and lets the customer cancel" and Control CTL-121 confirms "the overdraft fee prompt and cancel option appear before a fee-bearing transaction", which together satisfy the obligation's requirement to show the fee amount and give a choice to cancel before charging.

rows.text: A firm must send each consumer a monthly summary of all overdraft and returned-item fees charged in the previous month, with a year-to-date total.
rows.controlDesc: Monthly reconciliation that every account charged a fee received a fee summary with a year-to-date total
rows.reason: Policy POL-FEE-01 provides a monthly statement of all fees charged with a year-to-date total, but does not specifically limit this to overdraft and returned-item fees as required by the obligation.

rows.noticeTitle: Responding to customer data access requests
rows.text: A firm must respond to a customer data access request within 30 calendar days of receiving it, providing a copy of the personal data held.
rows.policyTitle: Privacy and Data Subject Rights Procedure
rows.controlDesc: Weekly report of data access requests open for more than 20 days, with escalation before the 30-day limit
rows.reason: Policy POL-PRV-01 states "Requests are answered within 30 calendar days" which matches the obligation's 30 calendar day deadline exactly, and Control CTL-131 escalates requests open for more than 20 days "before the 30-day limit" which would detect potential breaches of this specific obligation.

rows.noticeTitle: Responding to customer data access requests
rows.text: A firm must keep a log of every data access request, including the date received, the date answered and the outcome.
rows.policyTitle: Privacy and Data Subject Rights Procedure
rows.controlDesc: Weekly report of data access requests open for more than 20 days, with escalation before the 30-day limit
rows.reason: Policy POL-PRV-01 logs data access requests from customers with date received, date answered and outcome, but the obligation requires logging "every data access request" without limiting scope to customer requests only.

rows.noticeTitle: Operational resilience of important business services
rows.text: A firm must identify its important business services and set an impact tolerance for the maximum tolerable disruption of each.
rows.controlDesc: Annual Board approval of important business services and impact tolerances, recorded in Board minutes
rows.reason: Policy POL-RES-01 explicitly states "The bank maintains a list of important business services, each with an impact tolerance for maximum tolerable disruption" and Control CTL-141 ensures "Annual Board approval of important business services and impact tolerances," directly fulfilling both identification and impact tolerance setting requirements.

rows.noticeTitle: Operational resilience of important business services
rows.text: A firm must test its ability to remain within impact tolerance through severe but plausible scenario exercises at least once a year.
rows.controlDesc: Annual severe-but-plausible scenario test for each important business service, with results tracked
rows.reason: Policy POL-RES-01 states "Each service is tested against severe but plausible scenarios at least once a year" and Control CTL-142 implements "Annual severe-but-plausible scenario test for each important business service," which exactly matches the obligation's requirement to test ability to remain within impact tolerance through severe but plausible scenario exercises at least once a year.

rows.noticeTitle: Operational resilience of important business services
rows.text: The board must approve the list of important business services and impact tolerances each year.
rows.controlDesc: Annual Board approval of important business services and impact tolerances, recorded in Board minutes
rows.reason: Policy POL-RES-01 states "The Board approves the list and tolerances annually" and Control CTL-141 ensures "Annual Board approval of important business services and impact tolerances, recorded in Board minutes," which exactly matches the obligation's annual frequency requirement for board approval of both the list and impact tolerances.

rows.text: A firm must acknowledge a complaint in writing within 2 business days of receiving it.
rows.controlDesc: Daily report of complaints not acknowledged within 2 business days, reviewed by the complaints manager
rows.reason: Policy POL-CMP-01 requires "The complaints team acknowledges each complaint in writing within 2 business days" which exactly matches the obligation's 2 business day deadline, and Control CTL-101 generates a "Daily report of complaints not acknowledged within 2 business days" which would detect any breach of this specific obligation.

rows.text: A firm must send the customer a final response within 15 business days of receiving a complaint.
rows.controlDesc: Weekly report of complaints open for more than 30 calendar days without a final response, escalated to the head of Customer Care
rows.reason: Policy POL-CMP-01 requires a final response within 30 calendar days whereas the obligation mandates 15 business days, which is a longer deadline that does not meet the requirement.

rows.text: A firm must analyze the root causes of complaints at least quarterly and report the findings to senior management.
rows.controlDesc: Quarterly complaint root cause pack presented to the Executive Risk Committee, with owners for each fix
rows.reason: Policy POL-CMP-02 states "The complaints quality team groups complaints by product and cause every quarter" and "Findings and recommended fixes are presented to the Executive Risk Committee each quarter," which matches the obligation's requirement to analyze root causes at least quarterly and report findings to senior management, and Control CTL-103 confirms this by presenting the quarterly complaint root cause pack to the Executive Risk Committee.

rows.text: A firm must identify and verify every individual who owns 25 percent or more of a business customer before opening the account.
rows.controlDesc: Account opening system blocks business accounts until owners of 25 percent or more are verified
rows.reason: Policy POL-AML-01 states "For business customers, every individual owning 25 percent or more is identified and verified before account opening" and Control CTL-161 blocks business accounts until owners of 25 percent or more are verified, which exactly matches the obligation's threshold and timing requirement.

rows.text: A firm must refresh beneficial ownership information for high-risk business customers at least once a year.
rows.controlDesc: Monthly report of high-risk business customers whose beneficial ownership refresh is overdue
rows.reason: Policy POL-AML-01 states "Beneficial ownership for high-risk business customers is refreshed every year" which exactly matches the obligation's requirement of at least once a year, and CTL-162's monthly monitoring of overdue refreshes would detect breaches of this specific obligation.

rows.noticeTitle: Reimbursement for authorized push payment scams
rows.text: A firm must reimburse an eligible scam victim within 5 business days of the claim, unless it has evidence of gross negligence or first-party fraud.
rows.controlDesc: Weekly report of scam claims open for more than 5 business days
rows.reason: Policy POL-FRD-02 states "Eligible victims are reimbursed within 5 business days unless there is evidence of gross negligence or first-party fraud," which exactly matches the obligation's deadline and exceptions, and Control CTL-173 monitors compliance by reporting scam claims open for more than 5 business days.

rows.noticeTitle: Reimbursement for authorized push payment scams
rows.text: A firm must check the payee name against the account and show the customer a warning when the name does not match before a first payment to a new payee.
rows.controlDesc: Confirmation-of-payee check and name-mismatch warning tested in each app release
rows.reason: Policy POL-FRD-02 states "A confirmation-of-payee check runs before the first payment to a new payee, and a warning is shown when the name does not match," which exactly matches the obligation's requirements for timing, scope, and action.

rows.text: A firm must retain records of each complaint, including all correspondence with the customer, for at least 7 years from the final response.
rows.controlDesc: Weekly report of complaints open for more than 30 calendar days without a final response, escalated to the head of Customer Care
rows.reason: Policy POL-REC-01 requires customer communications including complaint correspondence to be deleted after 5 years, which is a shorter retention period than the 7 years required by the obligation, creating a direct conflict that prevents the obligation from being met.
rows.conflictReason: Policy A retains complaint files for 7 years after the final response (matching the obligation), but Policy B deletes customer communications including complaint correspondence after only 5 years from creation, which would violate the 7-year retention requirement for complaints.

rows.text: A firm must provide complaint records to the Authority within 10 business days of a request.
rows.controlDesc: Daily report of complaints not acknowledged within 2 business days, reviewed by the complaints manager
rows.reason: Policy POL-REC-02 states that regulatory requests are "answered within the deadline set by the supervisor, or within 10 business days if none is given," which matches the obligation's 10 business day requirement for providing complaint records to the Authority.

rows.text: A firm must notify the Financial Data Protection Office of a personal data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.
rows.controlDesc: Breach log review confirms supervisor notification within 72 hours for each reportable breach
rows.reason: Policy POL-PRV-02 states "The Privacy Office notifies the Financial Data Protection Office within 72 hours of the bank becoming aware of a breach," matching the obligation's 72-hour deadline exactly, and Control CTL-132 confirms "supervisor notification within 72 hours for each reportable breach."

rows.text: A firm must notify affected customers without undue delay when a breach is likely to put them at high risk.
rows.controlDesc: Monthly report of high-risk business customers whose beneficial ownership refresh is overdue
rows.reason: Policy POL-PRV-02 states "notifies affected customers without undue delay when the risk to them is high," which matches the obligation's requirement exactly.

rows.text: A firm must keep a register of third parties that support important business services.
rows.controlDesc: Supplier register completeness check for suppliers supporting important business services
rows.reason: Policy POL-TPR-01 states "All suppliers are recorded in the supplier register" and Control CTL-151 performs a "Supplier register completeness check for suppliers supporting important business services," which together ensure a register of third parties supporting important business services is maintained.

rows.text: A firm must maintain a tested exit plan for each critical third-party arrangement.
rows.controlDesc: Exit plan test for each critical supplier, every two years
rows.reason: POL-TPR-01 states "Each critical supplier has a documented exit plan that is tested every two years" and CTL-153 provides "Exit plan test for each critical supplier, every two years", which matches the obligation's requirement for a tested exit plan for each critical third-party arrangement.

rows.text: A firm must review the performance and risk of each critical third party at least once a year.
rows.controlDesc: Annual performance and risk review of each critical supplier
rows.reason: Policy POL-TPR-01 states "Suppliers that support important business services are reviewed for performance and risk at least once a year" and Control CTL-152 implements "Annual performance and risk review of each critical supplier", matching the obligation's requirement exactly.

rows.text: A firm must record, with the customer's consent, any vulnerability a customer discloses, so that staff can adapt how they serve that customer.
rows.controlDesc: Annual vulnerability training completion report for customer-facing colleagues
rows.reason: Policy POL-VUL-01 states "With the customer's consent, colleagues record disclosed vulnerabilities in the customer profile so service can be adapted," which exactly matches the obligation's requirement to record disclosed vulnerabilities with consent for service adaptation, and Control CTL-181 monitors this through quarterly review of vulnerability flags recorded with consent.

rows.text: A firm must train customer-facing staff to recognize and respond to signs of vulnerability at least once a year.
rows.controlDesc: Annual vulnerability training completion report for customer-facing colleagues
rows.reason: Policy POL-VUL-01 states "All customer-facing colleagues complete vulnerability training every year" which matches the obligation's requirement for training at least once a year, and Control CTL-182 monitors this through an "Annual vulnerability training completion report for customer-facing colleagues."

rows.noticeTitle: Third-party AI models in credit decisions
rows.text: A firm must maintain an inventory of third-party AI models used in consumer credit decisions, recording the supplier, purpose and the products affected.
rows.controlDesc: Monthly performance monitoring report for internally built credit scorecards
rows.reason: The obligation requires maintaining an inventory specifically of third-party AI models with supplier, purpose and affected products, but POL-TPR-01 only maintains a general supplier register with criticality ratings and POL-MRM-01 addresses only internally built models, neither capturing the required inventory of third-party AI models used in consumer credit decisions.

rows.noticeTitle: Third-party AI models in credit decisions
rows.text: The model risk committee must review each third-party AI model in the inventory at least once a year, including its performance and fairness results.
rows.controlDesc: Quarterly capital forecast reviewed by the Board Risk Committee
rows.reason: The obligation requires review of "each third-party AI model in the inventory" at least annually, but POL-MRM-01 only covers models "built by the bank" and POL-TPR-01 reviews "suppliers that support important business services" without specifically covering third-party AI models or their performance and fairness results.

rows.text: A firm must file a suspicious activity report within 30 calendar days of first detecting the suspicious activity.
rows.controlDesc: Weekly report of investigations approaching the 30-day filing deadline
rows.reason: Policy POL-AML-02 states "Suspicious activity reports are filed within 30 calendar days of first detection," which exactly matches the obligation's 30 calendar day deadline, and Control CTL-163 monitors "investigations approaching the 30-day filing deadline" to detect potential breaches.

rows.text: A firm must report suspicious activity reporting volumes and timeliness to the board at least quarterly.
rows.controlDesc: Quarterly suspicious activity reporting metrics presented to the Board Risk Committee
rows.reason: Policy POL-AML-02 states "Volumes and timeliness are reported to the Board Risk Committee each quarter" which matches the obligation's requirement to report suspicious activity reporting volumes and timeliness to the board at least quarterly, and Control CTL-164 implements this by presenting quarterly suspicious activity reporting metrics to the Board Risk Committee.

rows.text: A card issuer must show on each monthly statement how long it would take to repay the balance by paying only the minimum, and the total interest that would be paid.
rows.controlDesc: Statement template review confirms the minimum-payment warning, time to repay and total interest
rows.reason: Policy POL-CRD-01 requires monthly card statements to show "a minimum-payment warning with the time to repay and total interest if only the minimum is paid," which exactly matches the obligation's requirements, and Control CTL-191 confirms the presence of these elements.

rows.text: A firm must screen outgoing instant payments for fraud in real time, before the payment is released.
rows.controlDesc: Real-time fraud engine scores every outgoing instant payment before release; bypasses are logged and reviewed
rows.reason: Policy POL-FRD-01 states "Outgoing instant payments are scored by the real-time fraud engine before release" and Control CTL-171 confirms "Real-time fraud engine scores every outgoing instant payment before release", which exactly matches the obligation's requirement to screen outgoing instant payments for fraud in real time before release.

rows.text: A firm must give customers a way to report fraud that is available 24 hours a day, every day.
rows.controlDesc: Daily test call to the 24/7 fraud reporting line
rows.reason: Policy POL-FRD-01 states "Customers can report fraud by phone or in the app 24 hours a day, every day" which exactly matches the obligation's requirement, and CTL-172 performs a daily test call to verify the 24/7 fraud reporting line remains available.

rows.text: A firm must run liquidity stress tests at least monthly, including a scenario with rapid outflows of digital deposits.
rows.controlDesc: Monthly liquidity stress test results, including the digital outflow scenario, reviewed by ALCO
rows.reason: Policy POL-LIQ-01 states "Liquidity stress tests run monthly and include a rapid digital deposit outflow scenario" which exactly matches the obligation's frequency (at least monthly) and scope (including rapid digital deposit outflows), and Control CTL-211 ensures "Monthly liquidity stress test results, including the digital outflow scenario, reviewed by ALCO" which would detect any failure to run the required tests.

rows.text: A firm must hold enough liquid assets to cover the net outflows of its most severe stress scenario for at least 30 days.
rows.controlDesc: Daily check that liquid assets cover 30 days of net outflows in the most severe scenario
rows.reason: Policy POL-LIQ-01 states "The bank holds liquid assets sufficient to cover net outflows in its most severe scenario for at least 30 days" and Control CTL-212 performs a daily check that liquid assets cover 30 days of net outflows in the most severe scenario, which would detect any breach of the 30-day coverage requirement.

rows.text: An insurer or insurance intermediary must complete a written suitability assessment before recommending an annuity to a consumer.
rows.controlDesc: Security assessment sign-off before onboarding any cloud service holding customer data

rows.text: An insurer must disclose surrender charges and the surrender period before the consumer signs an annuity contract.
rows.controlDesc: App release test confirms the overdraft fee prompt and cancel option appear before a fee-bearing transaction

rows.noticeTitle: Best execution reporting for equity orders
rows.text: A broker-dealer must publish a quarterly report on the venues to which it routed customer equity orders and the execution quality obtained.
rows.controlDesc: Quarterly capital forecast reviewed by the Board Risk Committee

rows.text: A firm must offer statements and important notices in large print, braille or a screen-reader friendly format on request, at no extra cost.
rows.controlDesc: Monthly report of accessible-format requests and their fulfilment times
rows.reason: Policy POL-ACC-01 states "Statements and important notices are available in large print, braille and screen-reader friendly formats on request, free of charge" which precisely matches all requirements of the obligation, and Control CTL-183's monthly monitoring of accessible-format requests and fulfilment times would detect failures to provide these formats.

rows.text: A firm must keep a record of when and how each customer gave consent to electronic marketing.
rows.policy2Title: Privacy and Data Subject Rights Procedure
rows.controlDesc: Monthly check that marketing send lists exclude customers who withdrew consent
rows.reason: Policy POL-PRV-03 explicitly states "The date, channel and wording of each opt-in are stored in the consent register," which directly satisfies the obligation to keep a record of when and how each customer gave consent to electronic marketing.

rows.text: A firm must stop sending electronic marketing within 10 days after a customer withdraws consent.
rows.controlDesc: Monthly check that marketing send lists exclude customers who withdrew consent
rows.reason: Policy POL-PRV-03 requires withdrawals of consent to be applied within 5 days, which is shorter than the 10-day regulatory deadline.

rows.text: A firm must contact a mortgage borrower within 15 calendar days after a payment is missed.
rows.controlDesc: Daily arrears report confirms contact attempts within 10 days of a missed payment
rows.reason: Policy POL-MTG-01 requires contact within 10 calendar days, which is shorter than the 15 calendar days required by the obligation, and Control CTL-201 confirms these contact attempts within the same 10-day timeframe.

rows.text: A firm must offer a borrower in financial difficulty forbearance options, such as a temporary payment reduction, before starting repossession proceedings.
rows.controlDesc: Repossession checklist requires evidence that forbearance options were offered
rows.reason: Policy POL-MTG-01 explicitly states "Borrowers in financial difficulty are offered forbearance options, including temporary payment reductions and term extensions, before any repossession proceedings start" and Control CTL-202 requires evidence that forbearance options were offered before repossession.

rows.text: A firm must screen its customer base against each update to the sanctions list within 24 hours of the update being published.
rows.controlDesc: Rescreening job runs automatically within 24 hours of each sanctions list update, with completion logged
rows.reason: Policy POL-AML-03 states "When a sanctions list is updated, the full customer base is rescreened within 24 hours of publication" and Control CTL-165 confirms "Rescreening job runs automatically within 24 hours of each sanctions list update, with completion logged", both matching the obligation's 24-hour requirement exactly.

rows.text: A firm must report a significant cyber incident to the Prudential Banking Board within 24 hours of determining that the incident is significant.
rows.controlDesc: Breach log review confirms supervisor notification within 72 hours for each reportable breach
rows.reason: Policy POL-CYB-01 states "Significant cyber incidents are reported to the Prudential Banking Board within 24 hours of being classified as significant" which exactly matches the obligation's 24-hour deadline and scope, and Control CTL-221 confirms "supervisor notification within 24 hours of a significant classification" which would detect non-compliance with this specific reporting requirement.

rows.text: A firm must send the Prudential Banking Board a final incident report with root cause and remediation within 30 days after the incident is resolved.
rows.controlDesc: Final incident reports tracked to submission within 30 days of resolution
rows.reason: Policy POL-CYB-01 states "A final report with root cause and remediation follows within 30 days of resolution" and Control CTL-222 tracks "Final incident reports tracked to submission within 30 days of resolution," both matching the obligation's 30-day deadline and scope exactly.

rows.text: A firm must not call a consumer about a particular debt more than 7 times within 7 days.
rows.controlDesc: Dialer rule limits calls about one debt to 7 in 7 days; exceptions reviewed weekly
rows.reason: Policy POL-CRD-02 states "Calls about one debt are limited to 7 in any 7-day period" which matches the obligation's threshold exactly, and Control CTL-192 enforces this by limiting "calls about one debt to 7 in 7 days" with weekly exception reviews that would detect breaches.

rows.text: A firm must honor a consumer's request to be contacted only in writing.
rows.controlDesc: Monthly check that written-contact-only requests are flagged in the dialer
rows.reason: Policy POL-CRD-02 states "Requests to be contacted only in writing are recorded and honored" which directly meets the obligation, and CTL-193 monitors compliance by checking that written-contact-only requests are flagged in the dialer.

rows.text: A firm must post a notice in its app and on its website within 1 hour of an outage that prevents customers from making payments.
rows.controlDesc: Outage communication timestamps compared with outage start time after every payment outage
rows.reason: Policy POL-RES-03 requires Payments Operations to post a status message in the mobile app and on the website within 1 hour when customers cannot make payments, exactly matching the obligation's 1-hour deadline and scope, and Control CTL-143 verifies outage communication timestamps against outage start time after every payment outage, which would detect breaches of this specific obligation.

rows.text: A firm must give consumers at least 60 days' written notice before increasing a fee on a deposit account.
rows.controlDesc: Pricing change checklist confirms customer notices were sent at least 60 days before a fee increase
rows.reason: Policy POL-FEE-02 states "Customers are given at least 60 days' written notice before any fee on a deposit account increases" which exactly matches the obligation's 60-day written notice requirement, and Control CTL-123 confirms this by verifying "customer notices were sent at least 60 days before a fee increase."
